headline: Harmony is sounds working together—multiple notes creating richer textures than any could alone
universal_truth: Combination creates emergence; together, elements can produce what none could individually
fun_facts: The physics of harmony relates to simple ratios—octaves are exactly 2:1 frequency ratios
Western and Eastern musical traditions developed different harmonic systems independently
Dissonance isn't 'bad'—it creates tension that makes resolution feel satisfying
discussion_questions: Why do some note combinations sound 'pleasant' and others 'clashing'?
How is musical harmony like other forms of cooperation?
What in your life creates harmony when combined?

hook.script: One note is melody. Add a second note at the same time and something new appears: harmony. Some combinations sound peaceful, others tense, others rich. Multiple sounds interacting create something none could produce alone—musical chemistry.

cliff.script: Why do some note combinations sound 'right' and others 'wrong'? Is harmony just cultural preference, or is there something deeper?
cliff.prompt: Why do some harmonies sound pleasant?

options.text: Pleasant harmonies have simple mathematical ratios between their frequencies—our brains process them more easily
options.response: Yes. Octaves (2:1), fifths (3:2), and fourths (4:3) have simple ratios our brains recognize as 'consonant.' More complex ratios create 'dissonance'—not bad, just tension.

options.text: We learn which harmonies are pleasant from our musical culture
options.response: Culture shapes preference, but the mathematical basis of consonance appears universal...

fact1.title: Math in Music
fact1.script: Pythagoras discovered harmony's mathematics 2,500 years ago. Notes that sound good together have frequencies in simple ratios. Music isn't arbitrary—it's physics and math translated into emotion. Beauty has structure.

fact2.title: Tension and Release
fact2.script: Dissonance isn't error—it's tool. Composers use dissonance to create tension, then resolve to consonance for satisfaction. Without dissonance, harmony is flat. The journey between tension and release is what makes music emotional.

fact3.title: Cultural Variations
fact3.script: Different cultures developed different harmonic systems. Western music emphasizes thirds and triads. Indian ragas use different intervals. Middle Eastern music uses microtones Western music ignores. Harmony is universal; specific harmonies are cultural.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Combination creates emergence. Harmony teaches that together, elements can produce what none could individually. The right combinations make the whole greater than the sum of parts.

outro.script: That's Day 166. Tomorrow, we'll explore machines that make music—electronic instruments. Until then, listen for harmony in music—and in life.

growTrack.title: Harmony Recognition - Hear the Blend
growTrack.activity: Listen to a song with vocals and instruments. Try to hear how sounds blend—which notes support the melody? Where does tension build? Where does it resolve? Harmony is agreement; notice what happens when sounds work together.
